prs.title: Preserve the rendered shell on synchronous prerender abort
prs.author: gnoff
prs.body:
#37709 showed that a synchronous prerender abort can discard a retried task's rendered shell, then resume only an inner slot. #37710 addressed the missing markup by postponing the whole task, but that could overlap replay paths from child tasks; #37852 reverted that approach.

Preserve the parent segment and continue rendering its text and host elements after abort. When a component or other render callback returns after abort, discard its children and track a postponed hole at that node. This includes function and class components, lazy and forward-ref components, Context.Consumer render props, iterables, and thenables. Already-created arrays are read normally; getters and host prop serialization follow React's render-purity rules. SuspenseList rows use the same postponement path and existing row task bookkeeping.

Preserve individual holes only while rendering an unfinished Suspense boundary. Tasks without a blocked boundary unwind through the existing root abort path: a postponed root cannot flush any shell and must render again in full. Tests cover root aborts during the initial render, in a retried child, and during a subsequent resumeAndPrerender, followed by a complete final resume.

This restores the tests from #37710, #37850, and #37851 and adds coverage for indexed retries, static host children after abort, iterators and thenables, forward refs, render-phase updates, nested fallbacks, and SuspenseList rows. A full-flow regression for repeated aborts during resumeAnd

prs.title: Allow resumeAndPrerender to postpone an existing boundary again
prs.author: gnoff
prs.body:
`resumeAndPrerender` fails when the same already emitted Suspense boundary needs to postpone again. This predates #37853: prerendering a suspended boundary, aborting, resuming it while it still suspends, and aborting again hits the missing postponement metadata even when both aborts happen outside rendering.

Initialize tracking for resumed boundaries and preserve the boundary ID already referenced by the emitted HTML. When a pass finishes with postponed holes, flush completed segments as partial output and retain the fallback until a later resume completes the boundary.

Switch the full-flow regression from #37853 from `it.failing` to `it`, asserting prerender → resumeAndPrerender → final resume, intermediate HTML, JSON round trips, and removal of placeholders. Add a regression using external aborts to directly cover the existing API bug. Also verify that one resumed boundary can complete while a sibling aborts and postpones again, both at the root and through an already completed Suspense ancestor.

Follow-up to the merged #37853. This PR contains only the resumeAndPrerender fix and its regression tests.

The browser prerender suite passes in development and production on stable and experimental channels. ESLint and Prettier pass.

prs.title: [Fizz] Fix truncated prerender output under backpressure
prs.author: unstubbable
prs.body:
An aborted prerender can finish all tasks while partial output remains queued. If a Node stream applies backpressure, Fizz can close it before it flushes the remaining boundaries. This bug predates #37876 and also affects initial prerenders.

Fizz now waits for `partialBoundaries` to empty before it closes the destination. The regression test forces backpressure with `highWaterMark: 1` and verifies that `push()` returns `false`. Without the fix, the stream emits the first boundary's partial content and closes before it emits the second's.

prs.title: Ensure unique `useId` values in large trees
prs.author: eps1lon
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #37911
Closes https://github.com/react/react/pull/37912 (uses `slice()` which always allocates a new string)

When the tree position id exceeds 30 bits, `pushTreeContext` splits the low bits into a base 32 overflow string. The chunk is always a whole number of 5 bit groups, but `toString(32)` drops leading zero characters, erasing the boundary between the overflow digits and the remaining digits. Two structurally different tree positions could then serialize to the same id.

We now pad the overflow chunk with `padStart(numberOfOverflowBits / 5, '0')`. `padStart` short-circuits when the chunk is already full width, so the common case allocates nothing extra (it also beats a sentinel-bit plus `slice(1)` approach, which always allocates for these short strings).
